newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares leap 5.7 pct on local buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares leap 5.7 pct on local buying.

text.p: Indian stock markets began the new year on a bullish note on Wednesday with blue chips ending sharply higher on a flurry of local buying after the government said it would boost the country's capital markets, dealers said.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index jumped 175.86 points, or 5.70 percent, to a provisional close of 3,261.06 points, after reaching an intra-day high of 3,270.04.
The rally came after the government said on Tuesday it would propose a series of policy measures to boost the country's capital markets, traders said. The bombay bourse was closed on Tuesday.
"It's mainly a speculative bull run helped by a little bit of short-covering," said chief dealer Sanjeev Sanghvi at foreign brokerage James Capel B&K.
The government said it would announce policy measures this month to boost industrial growth and sagging markets.

"The government is likely to announce the decisions in early January," H.K. Dua, information adviser to the prime minister, told reporters at the end of a five-hour meeting between industrialists and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

Market participants said the good news came at a time of depressed sentiment and widespread concern about the slowdown in the economy. Hit by the gloomy outlook, the Bombay index fell to a three-year low of 2,713.12 in early December.

"Basically, the government has said it will take a broader look at the economy. This has given optimism for operators to pick up stocks," said Ashish Wakankar an institutional dealer at brokers Sundar Iyer.

The topics discussed between the government officials and industrialists were the revival of the capital market, credit availability, corporate taxation, delicensing and further opening of the economy, Dua said.
Expectations of increased fund allocations by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in Indian markets also led local players to build positions in frontline stocks.
"There is a little bit of anticipation of early FII allocations," said Capel's Sanghvi.
Dealers said speculators were active bidders in blue-chip stocks in anticipation of increased buying by foreign funds, which are the major players in the market.
Many foreign institutions were closed on New Year's day.
"People are doing front-running ... expecting foreign institutions to come into the market," said Vijay Pandya, chief dealer at Classic Share & Stock Brokers, a local firm.
"There are not many players around ... we are seeing moderate volumes in the market."
